issues.detail: The Greek 'αυτη' (this) refers back to a preceding concept (likely the knowledge of God), but the Vietnamese translates it as 'sự sống đời đời' (eternal life). More importantly, the Greek structure is 'This [the knowledge] IS eternal life IN ORDER THAT they might know...', whereas the Vietnamese renders it as 'Eternal life IS knowing Him...'. This shifts the grammatical role of 'eternal life' from the result/definition of the action to the subject of the sentence.
The Greek 'ινα' (in order that) expresses purpose, which is missing in the Vietnamese translation.
